item.title: Tech with Mak An AI agent can spend hundreds of generated tokens deciding betwee
item.description:
Tech with Mak
An AI agent can spend hundreds of generated tokens deciding between three tools. The actual decision can be represented by just three probabilities.

This is the idea behind Foundation Decision Models, and a new 52-page research paper from Nace AI explains how they are built and trained.

Consider a typical AI agent. It needs to decide whether to search the web, call a calculator, or respond directly. A generative language model produces text or structured JSON, which the application then parses to determine the next action.

A decision model approaches the problem differently.

It receives the current state, a question, and a set of possible answers. Instead of generating a response token by token, it returns a probability distribution over those answers.

This has important consequences for AI engineering.

The application can compare probabilities against thresholds, measure calibration, and escalate uncertain decisions. But probabilities also introduce challenges. Softmax does not guarantee calibrated confidence, and simply rearranging the available options should not change the decision.

The Nace AI researchers address these problems in their work on Drex.

One of the most interesting parts is Reinforcement Learning from Adjusted Feedback (RLAF).

For the open-weight Drex Max, training combines two sources of feedback:

→ Verified outcomes, when the correct answer can be established.

→ A generative Qwen3.8-27B judge that can perform extended reasoning before assigning probabilities to the options.

The decision model learns from this feedback through a reward objective, with KL regularization keeping its predictions close to the supervised checkpoint.

At inference, the model directly produces probabilities without generating the judge's reasoning.

The controlled ablation results are worth examining.

Decision Index score improved from 64.9 to 66.9, while choice accuracy increased from 86.5% to 88.0% after RLAF. A separate consistency ablation found that the rate of decisions changing under option reordering dropped from 6.3% to 4.2% when consistency losses were included.

And the broader development of decision models is already showing up in independent evaluations.

Drex Max v1.1 now ranks #1 among decision models on Artificial Analysis's Decision Index v2.1. It also sits on the performance-cost Pareto frontier at current published prices.

The paper documents the open-weight Drex family. The top-ranked v1.1 is a separate hosted model whose training details have not been disclosed.

There is a useful engineering distinction here. Generative models remain valuable for open-ended tasks, but tool routing, approval decisions, classification, and action selection can benefit from a model designed to return probabilities directly.

For an AI agent, knowing when to act and when to escalate can be just as important as choosing the correct action.

This week, Drex Max v1.1 is the #1 decision model on the @ArtificialAnlys Decision Index, out of 19, and on the Pareto frontier 🦖

72.6, above Jev 1.14, Claude Haiku 5.5 and GPT-6 Luna, on an index where 45% of the evaluation data is fully private and out of distribution.

$103 / 1M tasks, against $137 for the next-highest score.

#1 on AA-Paperclip, the heaviest part of the index: decisions and extraction over real documents.

On the Drex API: https://t.co/eTUlO9jyms - Nace AI
tweet

item.title: 外汇交易员 彭博社报道，总部位于中国内地和香港的机构投资者已被排除在Anthropic IPO的申购名单之外。部分潜在投资者仍在继续寻找参与认购的途径，但多家银
item.description:
外汇交易员
彭博社报道，总部位于中国内地和香港的机构投资者已被排除在Anthropic IPO的申购名单之外。部分潜在投资者仍在继续寻找参与认购的途径，但多家银行要么已拒绝接受此类订单，要么认为这些投资者几乎不可能获得配售。

分析指，这些限制在一定程度上是受美国《国际武器贸易条例》（ITAR）的影响，该条例旨在管控防务产品的贸易，情况与SpaceX IPO类似，不过两地的投资者在SpaceX上市后可以在二级市场买入。

周五，香港地区已可以正常浏览路演演示文稿，但香港本地的零售券商并未被列入授权分销商名单。
https://t.co/4UwVl3oOOi

彭博：中国内地于香港投资者被禁止参与本次SpaceX IPO认购，理由是美国对关键技术出口有限制。限制源于美国《国际武器贸易条例（ITAR）》，涉及国防相关技术和技术数据的出口。

另外，目前SpaceX官网已禁止内地与香港用户访问。 https://t.co/nffUyITAfU - 外汇交易员
tweet
